chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, who said:

I saw Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) in the courtyard of the Ka'bah at night, and he was praying. He prolonged the standing until he would lean on his right leg at one time, and on his left leg at another time. Then I heard him saying in a voice as if he were crying.
O my Master! Will You punish me while Your love is in my heart? By Your might, if You do so, You will surely gather me and the people with whom I have long been an enemy for Your sake.
ai.seo_question: What was the supplication of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) while praying in the courtyard of the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual intensity of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) during his prolonged night prayer (Qiyam) at the Ka'bah, illustrating the Shia concept of 'Ishq' (divine love) as a sufficient justification for salvation. His supplication reflects the theological principle that love for God and His Prophet serves as a protective shield against punishment, a theme deeply rooted in Shia exegetical tradition. The physical signs of exhaustion—leaning on his legs—underscore the depth of his devotion and the reality of his connection with the Divine.
